analysis:
Examined the three changed files. ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (head 15-71): adds noteCoordinatorRequest, which records lastRequestAt on the live coordinatorConnection, guarded to connected==true (line 18). noteCoordinatorConnection rebuilds the struct on each connect/disconnect, so lastRequestAt resets per connection (lines 10-12). superviseServingAuthorization now uses ServingReadiness.verdict(connection, trust, now) in place of the inline hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization/legacy check (line 31). Its results drive only local logging and the planned re-registration via requestPlannedReconnect (line 62), which is gated by UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery backoff and the busy/update idle check (lines 54-57, 69-71). This is local supervision, not an admission or serving gate. Per TB-011/T-053, the coordinator remains authoritative for grants, and a provider-side verdict grants nothing. Worst case for a misjudged verdict is too few or too many self-initiated reconnects; backoff bounds this as an availability concern (A-018).

ProviderLoop+Trust.swift line 157 adds an injectable receivedAt with a default of now. The value is diagnostic only.

DaemonStateFile.swift head 338-345 adds an optional lastRequestAt to CoordinatorConnection. Older state files still decode, and the schema is unchanged. The new field adds no sensitive data, only a timestamp in the owner-written state file.

No regression identified against TB-011, T-053, A-016 or A-018.

Open questions for integration:
1) The ServingReadiness.verdict implementation is not supplied. Check whether a recent lastRequestAt can mask a blocked or expired-authorization verdict, and whether anything gates admission on this verdict rather than only on logging and reconnect.
2) Find the callers of noteCoordinatorRequest. Confirm it fires only for coordinator-routed requests on the current connection, not local-endpoint requests.
3) Determine which callers pass receivedAt to handleTrustStatus. Confirm none can backdate or forward-date trust status to extend apparent authorization freshness in status/doctor output.
